title: QBR - Elysia Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check covering April usage, cost hotspots, recent reliability incident and mitigation, roadmap ask for private deployment exploration, and agreed next steps to run a perf benchmark and share enterprise pricing + security pack.
transcript:
[00:00] Alice Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're running about 42 minutes today for the QBR, quick intro - I'm Alice from Redwood, Miguel is our SE, Priya from CSM.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Sounds good, Samir here, CTO at Elysia Health, Jenna and Ravi are with me, Lena from compliance will join for the security bits.
[00:25] Miguel Ortega: Great, we'll start with usage and cost, then reliability and incidents, then roadmap. Miguel: quick note, some of the numbers below are from the usage report we sent last week (link: https://redwood.share/elysia/qbr-apr).
[00:38] Miguel Ortega: In April you averaged ~1.4M tokens/day for chat generation and 220k embed units/week, cost steady mid-month then spiked the week of 4/12.
[00:52] Jenna Park: yeah that spike was from our nightly batch reranking job, we kicked off a new dataset and didn't have caching set up so it re-generated a lot.
[01:05] Miguel Ortega: Right, the batch was long sequences which bypassed prefix cache, plus disable batching in the job config meant you lost batching gains. We estimated that enabled batching + prefix cache would cut that spike by ~55-65%.
[01:20] Ravi Menon: Do you have suggested config changes? We tried the quick config in the docs but unclear on autoscale implications.
[01:31] Miguel Ortega: For your workload I'd recommend enabling continuous batching on the Dedicated pool or using Redwood Hosted with suggestion to enable adaptive batching. Also set a max sequence cap for the batch job and use the prefix cache key - I'll send an example config.
[01:45] Alice Chen: On cost, Priya can share a per-route cost breakdown and a couple pricing levers: reserved dedicated capacity vs burst, and token-level optimizations like quantization and response length caps.
[01:58] Priya Rao: Yes - current month ARR-equivalent usage would justify a small reserved commitment. We ran a simulated commit and showed ~23% unit cost reduction at the 6mo reserved level, details in the pricing model sheet (link: https://redwood.share/elysia/pricing-model).
[02:12] Jenna Park: We need to balance cost with latency - patient messaging can't tolerate >500ms response tail. Our 95th percentile is around 420ms now but occasional tail spikes.
[02:26] Miguel Ortega: We saw two tail spikes in April tied to autoscaler cold-starts during heavy ingest windows. One was 4/12 at 03:14 UTC and another 4/22 14:03 UTC. Both were mitigated by fallback to a smaller model variant but resulted in increased token cost.
[02:43] Samir Patel: Can you explain the fallback behavior? We saw unexpected model changes in logs.
[02:49] Miguel Ortega: Sure. Policy routing will try the primary model, if capacity constrained or latency SLO threatened we fallback to a compatible variant. In your case the primary was a quantized Llama variant and fallback went to a smaller unquantized variant which increased downstream token counts. We can tune thresholds.
[03:05] Lena Ortiz: On compliance - quick question: do you keep audit logs for inference requests longer than 90 days? Our policy requires 12 months for certain flows.
[03:16] Alice Chen: Standard retention is 90 days on hosted, but for Private deployments or Enterprise add-on we can configure longer retention and integrate with your SIEM via the audit log export. We'll include options in the security pack.
[03:30] Lena Ortiz: Also SOC 2 attestation and KMS/HSM key control - what's the current status?
[03:36] Priya Rao: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we offer KMS integrations for Private. We'll attach the SOC 2 report and the KMS integration guide.
[03:46] Jenna Park: For our PII-adjacent flows we might need VPC or an on-prem option. What's the gating timeline?
[03:54] Miguel Ortega: Private deployments can be onboarded in 8-12 weeks typically, depending on infra support and the depth of KMS/HSM integration. We also offer a hybrid private control plane that keeps data in your VPC.
[04:07] Samir Patel: Reliability - we had that one incident on 3/22 where a scheduler bug caused a 12-min degradation. What was the RCA?
[04:16] Miguel Ortega: That incident was a scale-down race condition in the autoscaler where KV cache warmups were dropped; our team deployed a fix on 3/23 and we rolled a hotfix to ensure warmup completes before scale-down. The engineering postmortem is in the shared folder (link: https://redwood.share/elysia/rca-0322).
[04:33] Samir Patel: Ok thanks, did that change affect cost?
[04:36] Miguel Ortega: Minimal, the hotfix added a short warmup window but prevented repeated cold starts which were more costly.
[04:43] Jenna Park: We're also seeing occasional hallucination regressions in the medical Q&A model - has Redwood observed distribution shifts?
[04:52] Miguel Ortega: We monitor quality via eval sets; we did see a small regression after the 4/04 model merge. Recommended path is to pin a previous model for high-risk flows or run a canary with differential testing. We can set up automated evals for your prompt set.
[05:07] Priya Rao: Actionable step - we'll run an eval sweep across your 120 prompt test set and share results by next Wednesday.
[05:15] Alice Chen: On roadmap, Elysia mentioned exploring an on-prem or VPC deployment for regulatory flows. How should we prioritize?
[05:24] Samir Patel: High priority for patient-facing transcripts, medium for analytics. Timeline Q3 if possible.
[05:31] Miguel Ortega: We can propose a hybrid plan: move sensitive flows to Private and keep analytics on Redwood Hosted. We'll draft a migration plan and resource estimate.
[05:42] Ravi Menon: For the private plan, are there special infra reqs? We run GKE and have strict firewall rules.
[05:49] Miguel Ortega: GKE is supported, we'll need to coordinate peering, NAT, and KMS network paths. We'll send a checklist for infra prerequisites.
[06:00] Alice Chen: Let's review open action items and next steps - Priya, Miguel, Samir, can we confirm owners.
[06:08] Priya Rao: I'll take the pricing / reserved capacity proposal and attach the simulated savings. Due 2026-05-11.
[06:15] Miguel Ortega: I'll own the perf benchmark and configuration examples for batching/prefix cache. Due 2026-05-14. I'll also run the 120-prompt eval and share results.
[06:25] Samir Patel: I'll sync internally on timeline and confirm stakeholders for private deployment, reply by 2026-05-08.
[06:33] Lena Ortiz: I'll review the SOC 2 and KMS docs once you share.
[06:38] Alice Chen: Any other blockers?
[06:41] Jenna Park: One ask - can Redwood run a 72-hr load test to validate tail latency under our peak pattern?
[06:48] Miguel Ortega: Yes, we can run a controlled load test with you on a staging pool; will need a target window. We'll schedule after perf config is agreed.
[06:58] Alice Chen: Great, recap: pricing proposal, perf configs + benchmark, eval sweep results, infra checklist and security pack. We'll send calendar invites for a technical deep dive.
[07:12] Samir Patel: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[07:18] Alice Chen: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:22] [meeting ended]
action_items: Priya Rao: Prepare reserved capacity pricing proposal + savings model; due 2026-05-11
Miguel Ortega: Run perf benchmark, provide batching/prefix-cache config examples, and run 120-prompt eval; due 2026-05-14
Samir Patel: Confirm internal stakeholders and timeline for Private deployment; due 2026-05-08
Redwood: Share SOC 2 report, KMS integration guide, and security pack link; due 2026-05-06
Miguel Ortega: Schedule 72-hour staging load test window with Elysia once perf config agreed; target week of 2026-05-18
next_steps: Share perf benchmark results and config snippets (Miguel)
Deliver eval sweep results on 120 prompt set (Miguel)
Provide infra checklist for Private deployment (SE team)
Schedule technical deep dive and load test window
